profiles.hook: Dixon became Chancellor of North Carolina Central University in 2024 after leading Elizabeth City State University for over eight years, including as interim and then permanent Chancellor, and after six years overseeing academic and student affairs system-wide for the 17-campus University of North Carolina system. Her research has focused on college access and summer bridge programs.

profiles.hook: Arbaugh went from a diving accident that left him paralyzed to becoming, at 29, the first person on Earth to use a brain implant to control a computer in daily life, turning his own recovery into the most closely watched real-world test of whether brain-computer interfaces can restore independence.
profiles.name: Noland Arbaugh

quote.text: This is going to change the world for so many people, and it's already changing my life.
quote.context: Noland Arbaugh, in a Neuralink livestream demonstration, March 2024

primary.name: Neuralink PRIME Study, official trial information
Noland Arbaugh: 'This is what happens when you get the future you dreamed of,' The Wall Street Journal interview (2024)

secondary.name: Elon Musk's Neuralink Implants Its First Device in a Human Brain, The New York Times (2024)

timeline.event: Diving accident results in paralysis below the shoulders
timeline.impact: Life-altering spinal cord injury

timeline.event: Receives the first Neuralink implant in January
timeline.impact: First human recipient of the device

timeline.event: Livestreams playing chess using the implant
timeline.impact: Public proof-of-concept demonstration reaches wide audience

quick_facts: First human recipient of Neuralink's implanted brain-computer interface (January 2024)
Paralyzed from the shoulders down after a 2016 diving accident
Publicly demonstrated controlling a computer cursor and playing video games using thought alone
Became a public advocate for brain-computer interface technology and disability accessibility

achievements.title: First human Neuralink implant recipient (January 2024)
achievements.impact: Became the first person to receive Neuralink's N1 brain-computer interface implant, a milestone clinical trial event for the BCI field.

achievements.title: Public demonstration of thought-controlled computer use
achievements.impact: Livestreamed playing chess and video games using only his implant to control a cursor, providing the most visible public proof-of-concept for consumer BCI technology to date.

achievements.title: Continued long-term use of the implant through device issues
achievements.impact: Publicly documented a partial signal loss and the team's fix, providing an unusually transparent real-world account of BCI reliability challenges.

achievements.title: Public advocacy for disability and BCI access
achievements.impact: Used his platform to advocate for expanded brain-computer interface trials and greater independence for people with paralysis.
